Hotel service work

Open each checklist to see the details I verify before finishing a task.

Housekeeping

Guest-room turnover

Reset a departure room and report its status for the next arrival.

View room checklist
  • Replace used linen, replenish amenities, and check key surfaces and the bathroom.
  • Flag maintenance issues and report the room status after the final inspection.

Banquet rotation

Event room setup

Set tables to the agreed floor plan before the banquet team opens the room.

View setup checklist
  • Match the cover count and arrange linen, place settings, and water stations.
  • Walk the guest routes to check clearance and raise last-minute changes with the banquet captain.

Food & beverage rotation

Room-service tray setup

Prepare and check a tray with the service team before dispatch.

View tray checklist
  • Match the items, covers, cutlery, and condiments to the order.
  • Check any dietary notes with the service lead and confirm the delivery handoff.

Guest support

A guest-request round

Restock the trolley and follow through on requests for towels or amenities.

View handover checklist
  • Confirm the requested items and update the service log after delivery.
  • Give the next shift any open request, the responsible team, and the promised follow-up time.

Training & service scenarios

Hotel operations placement

Housekeeping trainee · 2025. Supported room resets, linen control, and inspection handovers, with short rotations in banquets and food service.

Practice scenario · A room fails its final check

I’d keep the room pending, notify the supervisor and front desk, replace the missing items, then request a final recheck before the room is released.

Hospitality operations training

Certificate coursework · 2024–2025. Guest-room standards, equipment handling, service setup, guest communication, and safety reporting.

Practice scenario · A spill just before doors open

I’d alert the banquet captain, mark the affected area, and direct guests to a clear route while the designated team clears the spill. I’d check with the captain before reopening the walkway.
